item.title: Evan Williams named NFC defensive player of the month
item.description: Packers safety Evan Williams has been named NFC defensive player of the month for October.
item.content:encoded:
Packers safety Evan Williams has been named NFC defensive player of the month for October.

In his third season, Williams has helped elevate Green Bay’s defense this year. He had 41 total tackles with four passes defensed, two interceptions, a sack, and a fumble recovery last month.

According to the league, Williams is the third safety since 2000 to tally at least 40 tackles and three takeaways in a single month. He’s the first to accomplish the feat since 2011.

This is Williams’ first defensive player of the month award.

In eight games this season, Williams has totaled 71 tackles, two tackles for loss, four QB hits, six passes defensed, and two interceptions.

item.title: Malik Nabers named NFC offensive player of the month
item.description: Giants receiver Malik Nabers had a strong October and now has been recognized for it.
item.content:encoded:
Giants receiver Malik Nabers had a strong October and now has been recognized for it.

The NFL named Nabers NFC offensive player of the month.

He had 36 catches for a league-high 509 yards with two touchdowns in October.

As noted by the league, Nabers was No. 2 with 36 receptions last month and was the only player to record at least 100 receiving yards in four games.

This is Nabers’ first career player of the month award.

In seven games this year, Nabers has caught 48 passes for 605 yards with two touchdowns.

item.title: Drake Maye is the AFC offensive player of the month
item.description: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye heard a lot of criticism in September, but it faded away in October.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye heard a lot of criticism in September, but it faded away in October.

After throwing six interceptions during a 1-2 start to the season, Maye guided the Patriots to a 3-1 mark last month. Maye threw multiple touchdowns in all four of New England's games, including four in the team's win over the Raiders.

He was 90-of-134 for 1,199 yards, 12 touchdowns and two interceptions in those games and he also ran 23 times for 129 yards and two more scores.

The NFL announced on Wednesday that they have named Maye the AFC offensive player of the month. It's the first time he has received the award.

item.title: Where can I watch the Dolphins vs. Lions game?
item.description: The Lions at Dolphins game will be seen in a small part of Florida and in all of the NFC North markets.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins host the Detroit Lions in Week 9, kicking off on Sunday afternoon from Hard Rock Stadium. Miami lost in Week 8, dropping to 1-6 in a season that is focused on establishing a foundation for a rebuilding team. The Lions are coming off a win to give their NFC North rivals, the Minnesota Vikings, their first loss of the year. Detroit is 5-2 this season, but third in their division. After a disappointing 9-8 season last year, the Lions are looking to fight their way back to the top of the NFC North in route to another deep playoff run.

This is a game between a team that is likely headed toward an early pick in the 2027 NFL Draft and a team hoping to be a factor in the NFC postseason. The television broadcast plan seems to mirror exactly who each team is.

Reminder: Affiliates can elect to change their coverage assignments during the week – we will update on Sunday if there are any changes to the Dolphins’ viewing area.

Where will the Lions vs. Dolphins game air on TV?

The good news about the broadcast plan for this week is CBS has assigned Kevin Harlan and Trent Green to the coverage. Harlan’s play-by-play call is becoming legendary in Miami, and we will once again get to experience it on Sunday.

The bad news is, not much of Florida will receive the game on their local CBS channel. With Miami struggling, only the Miami, West Palm Beach, and Fort Myers markets will get the game.

As for the markets interested in the game because of the Lions side of the schedule, all of the NFC North will get to watch. All of Michigan and Wisconsin will air the game, along with most of Minnesota. The Chicago market in northern Illinois and Indiana will pick up the game, as will the Toledo, Ohio CBS affiliate.

.

What other games will I see in Florida?

1 p.m. Eastern time slot

On CBS, most of the state will see the New York Jets at Kansas City Chiefs game, while Tampa will air the Denver Broncos at Carolina Panthers game and the western end of the Panhandle will have the Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints game.

FOX has the doubleheader this week and will start with the Dallas Cowboys at Indianapolis Colts game throughout most of Florida. The New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles game is expected to be shown in Miami and West Palm Beach.

4:05/4:25 p.m. Eastern time slot

The second game on FOX will be the Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots game throughout all of Florida.

8:20 p.m. Eastern time slot – Sunday Night Football

The Sunday Night Football game this weekend will feature the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at the Chicago Bears.

We're gearing up for Week 9 of the NFL season (and the looming NFL trade deadline), where teams will have to make a decision on the intended course of the remainder of their season — are they going all in? Or is it time to tear it all down and look toward the future?

One of those teams will be the Baltimore Ravens (4-4), whose quarterback, Lamar Jackson, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery and has landed him on injured reserve. Backup Tyler Huntley then suffered what is reportedly a season-ending turf toe injury in relief of Jackson, putting undrafted free agent Joe Fagnano into action as the emergency third quarterback.

Now, Fagnano will get the start as the Jacksonville Jaguars travel to face the Ravens on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 9. The 25-year-old, who played his college ball at Maine and then UConn, will be the second undrafted rookie to start under center for Baltimore in the Ravens' 32-year history, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley.

NFL fans also await news on the fate of star running back Jonathan Taylor, who has been touted as a potential trade-deadline mover as the Indianapolis Colts kicked off their franchise reset with a fire sale. They've already traded away two foundational players, Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, for several draft picks as they look to the future, leaving us to wonder whether their star running back could be next.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more ahead of Week 9.

item.title: Can J.J. McCarthy become the NFL’s next reclamation QB — and lead the Giants to the playoffs?
item.description: Minnesota gave up on its 2024 No. 10 pick for a fifth-rounder. Since coming off the bench in Week 6, McCarthy has thrown for 495 yards in five quarters and led the NFC East-leading Giants to an overtime win at Houston. Even Vic Fangio is calling him a steal.
item.content:encoded:
There is now a fairly common, if somewhat circuitous, path to quarterback success in the NFL.

Get drafted high by your first NFL team, bomb out with that team for whatever reasons, wander the desert as a backup with other franchises for a while, find the right environment after all you’ve learned, and whammo — all of a sudden, you’re a credible starting quarterback!

It’s worked in the last few years for Geno Smith, Baker Mayfield, Sam Darnold, and Daniel Jones, and J.J. McCarthy may be the next name on the list.

The Minnesota Vikings selected McCarthy with the 10th overall pick in the 2024 draft — in fact, they traded up to do so — and it never worked out. Between injuries and McCarthy’s own lack of development and established skills as an NFL-level prospect, it became very clear that Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell — one of the brightest offensive minds in the league, and the man who had helped to facilitate Darnold’s and Jones’ career turnarounds — would not be the one to transform McCarthy from college game manager (McCarthy’s Michigan teams were led by great defense and a powerful rushing attack) to NFL franchise guy.

Which is why the Vikings traded McCarthy to the Giants on September 28 for a 2027 fifth-round pick. That’s how far McCarthy’s stock had fallen — he was the team’s third-string quarterback behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz — and the Giants were just trying to settle things at the game’s most important position after Jaxson Dart suffered meniscus and MCL injuries in his left knee in Week 2 against the Los Angeles Rams. Suddenly, Big Blue needed depth behind Jameis Winston, and McCarthy just needed a fresh start.

That fresh start came quite unexpectedly in the Giants’ 34-27 Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints. Winston threw an interception with 12:28 left in the game, and the G-Men were down 34-10 after putting up a 10-0 early lead. Head coach John Harbaugh put McCarthy in to get some kind of spark going, not suspecting that he was unleashing something far more nuclear in nature. In less than a full fourth quarter, McCarthy completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown, one interception, and a passer rating of 90.0. He wasn’t doing this with quick throws and yards after the catch — McCarthy had several explosive downfield throws that were right on the money.

McCarthy made Secret Superstars in Week 6 for that performance, and he was named the starter for the Giants’ Week 7 game against the Houston Texans. DeMeco Ryans’ Texans defense is not what it was in 2025 — perhaps the NFL’s best — but it was still a serious test.

Which McCarthy passed with relatively flying colors. He was eager to show off what he had learned, and McCarthy’s connection with offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, and passing game coordinator/quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan. Very few people were excited about those hires this past offseason, but it’s all worked out very well in McCarthy’s favor.

Against the Texans, McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards, no touchdowns, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 99.1 in a 27-21 overtime win. The Giants leaned heavily on the run game, but McCarthy was throwing darts again. Moreover, you started to see the development of the route concepts, and how they helped McCarthy do what he can at this point in his career.

Not that O’Connell didn’t build concepts for his quarterbacks — of course he did — but sometimes, a new environment makes all the difference.

“Preparation,” McCarthy said after the Texans game, when asked how the tight-window throws have been such a big part of his recent performances. “I feel like preparation, over the years of playing football, you just refine the routine each and every week. I feel like I’m in a really good spot right now, just Monday through Saturday and just being able to have that trust in these guys as early as now, since I’ve been here. I haven’t been here long, but I trust those guys every time the ball comes out of my hand. I trust the offensive line up front. I trust the backs are going to get us in great situations when I do hit the checkdowns, but at the end of the day, it’s the players around me.”

Now, the 4-2-1 Giants prepare to face a 2-6 Philadelphia Eagles team that has been an epic disappointment for all kinds of reasons, and the extent to which Vic Fangio’s defense has fallen down is truly surprising. On Tuesday, Fangio spoke about the Giants, and about McCarthy specifically.

“They’ve got a really good offense. They’ve got skill at the receiving position. They did a nice job raiding the Ravens, not only for John [Harbaugh], but for [TE Isaiah] Likely and [FB Patrick] Ricard. They’ve got a lot of the Ravens-type offense that they had when Greg [Roman] was there, and they’ve intermixed Kansas City-type passing in there with Matt [Nagy]. They’ve got it going right now. They’ve got good wideouts, good tight ends, two good backs. The quarterback has come in, in a short period of time, and really done a nice job, for them to get him for a [fifth-round] pick is a steal.”

If McCarthy continues to tell his own reclamation story this season, and even leads the NFC East-leading Giants to the playoffs for the first time since the 2022 season, it will open up a new chapter in his career.

For now, Harbaugh and his crew will just enjoy the unexpected benefits.

item.title: NFL predictions: Will Liam Coen school Jesse Minter yet again?
item.description: Coen’s offenses have scored over 30 points every time he’s faced Minter.
item.content:encoded:
We’re previewing THURSDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL, y’all! Get excited!

Here are some predictions for what we’ll see tonight when the 5-2 Jacksonville Jaguars take on the 4-4 Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium.

Prediction #1

The good news is that the Ravens will not have an NFL-caliber quarterback on the field on Thursday night.

Two-time MVP Lamar Jackson (thumb) and familiar backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley (toe) are both on injured reserve. Baltimore attempted to salvage its season by trading for veteran pocket passer Jacoby Brissett, but he won’t be available for this Week 9 matchup on a short week. The Jaguars will be facing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who posted a 40.0 passer rating in his first NFL action last week. Lucky us.

The bad news is that the Ravens still have Derrick Henry.

The Yulee native has rushed for the most yards (1,564) and touchdowns (16) of any NFL player against Jacksonville. Henry has six career games of 120+ rushing yards and at least 1 touchdown against the Jaguars. He had that one 99-yard play where he—

I don’t need to remind y’all. It’s been 1,033 days since Henry last faced his hometown team (and the same amount of time since he suited up for the Tennessee Titans), but we all know that he’s one of the few non-quarterbacks in the league who can put an offense entirely on his shoulders.

This will be the Jaguars’ first matchup against Henry in a Ravens uniform. While Jacksonville will surely miss defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton, Jackson’s absence is a far greater factor. Henry averages 4.5 yards per carry and is stuffed on 16.0% of rushes with Jackson on the field this season, compared to 3.5 yards per carry and a 22.9% stuff rate without Jackson, per NFL Pro.

Over the past three weeks, a span in which Jackson played 1 offensive snap, Henry was hit behind the line of scrimmage at the league’s highest rate (60.0%). He averages a league-worst 0.8 yards per carry on such plays this season, compared to 6.2 yards per carry when he is not contacted in the backfield.

Even with the Ravens starting an undrafted rookie at quarterback, the Jaguars will need a sound strategy to contain wide receiver Zay Flowers… but the top priority in the defensive game plan this week should be preventing Henry from hitting his stride.

The prediction: Derrick Henrygets stuffed repeatedly, finishes with under 50 yards

Henry’s rushing over/under prop is set at 68.5 yards on FanDuel.

Prediction #2

On the other side of the ball, Jacksonville is as close to full-strength as it can get. Trevor Lawrence is operating the offense at an MVP-caliber level; skill players are taking turns having breakout games; and the offensive line is doing juuuuust fine.

The obvious driver of Jacksonville’s success is its head coach and offensive playcaller, Liam Coen. He’s been in a Steph Curry-like flow state for much of the season. The Jaguars have scored 30+ points in four of seven games, including each of their past two outings, and their +85 point differential leads the league by a country mile.

Ravens fans would probably like to see their head coach and defensive playcaller, Jesse Minter, be viewed as the defensive version of Coen. A young, innovative mind who can lead a locker room just as well as he can devise a game plan.

However, in two career meetings between a Coen offense and a Minter defense, the former coach had far more success.

In Week 7 of 2024, Coen called the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ offense, and Minter called the Ravens’ defense (as defensive coordinator). The Bucs converted 12/18 late downs, produced 481 yards of offense, and scored 31 points.

In Week 11 of 2025, Coen called the Jaguars’ offense, and Minter called the Los Angeles Chargers’ defense. The Jags converted 8/15 late downs, produced 345 yards of offense, and scored 35 points.

Is Minter really going to be the guy to stop this freight train?

The prediction: Liam Coen’s offense scores 30 or more points yet again

Jacksonville’s team total is set at 24.5 points on FanDuel.

Prediction #3

The Jaguars are incentivized to get Brian Thomas Jr. going.

As many are quick to point out, the NFL is a “what have you done for me lately?” league. A few good games from Thomas could boost his trade value and convince another team to acquire him for significant draft capital.

But the Jaguars should want Thomas to stack strong performances, regardless of their interest in trading him. We’ve all seen what he’s capable of on an NFL field. The best-case scenario for Jacksonville isn’t “Thomas plays well enough that we can trade him for a haul.” The best-case scenario would be “Thomas plays well enough that he refinds his groove and helps make our offense as dangerous as possible.”

Both of his touchdowns this season came in the redzone. According to NFL Pro, Thomas has run a deep route on 3.3 plays per game, compared to 5.1 deep routes per game in 2024 and 5.9 in 2025. He only has 3 deep targets this season and has not caught any.

This week looks like a good matchup, though. Baltimore’s defense ranks bottom three in completion percentage (65.1%) and EPA per attempt (0.67) allowed on downfield passes. Minter’s unit has also allowed in-breaking passes to be wide open by 5+ yards of separation at a league-worst 24.8% rate. Can we get a deep post from BT, pretty please?

The prediction: Brian Thomas Jr. scores his first long touchdown of 2026

Thomas’ receiving over/under prop is set at 12.5 yards on FanDuel. He has +550 odds to score a touchdown.

item.title: What to know about Falcons – Bengals in Week 9
item.description: The Falcons are facing a tough matchup in Madrid against a high-flying Bengals team.
item.content:encoded:
From rain in Florida to sunny skies in Spain, from a punishing rushing attack to a high-flying aerial assault, from a division rival to an AFC powerhouse in the making. The Falcons are facing a very different kind of challenge in very different circumstances this week, and they must be ready to rise and face that challenge after a sloppy, stupid loss against the Buccaneers in Week 8.

What do the Bengals bring to the table? How will the Falcons have to attack this game if they’re going to win? Here’s a primer for Week 9’s big game in Madrid.

Team rankings

The Falcons can run the ball better than the Bengals and are less inclined to let offenses march up and down the field on them—though maybe not after last week!—but Cincinnati outclasses them virtually everywhere else. Their passing game is elite, they’re better at not turning the ball over, and they’re better at forcing turnovers, all of which will make life difficult on Sunday.

The Falcons just don’t have the profile of a good team right now, both based on their up-and-down play and their broad statistical profile. We’ll see if they can buck that this week.

How the Bengals have changed

We haven’t seen the Bengals in a while—these two teams last played in 2022—but we’ll just focus on this offseason.

The biggest move was a loss, as the Bengals let Trey Hendrickson walk to the division rival Ravens. They made up for that by trading their first round pick for Lawrence, who has absolutely kicked ass, and adding Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, and Bryan Cook to the defense. Their offensive additions were essentially a pair of new starting offensive linemen in tackle Orlando Brown Jr. and guard Dalton Risner, and every one of their draft picks is currently a backup, though some of them have considerable promise. There’s a real high-ceiling nucleus here already, though, so the additions at key positions have clearly put the Bengals in a better spot this year, so long as Burrow stays healthy.

What to know about Week 9

This is almost the exact opposite of the challenge the Buccaneers presented in Week 8. The Falcons will have agreeable weather in Madrid, more than likely, but they’ll face a Bengals team with a weak rushing attack, weak run defense, and excellent passing game.

That’s playing into Atlanta’s relative strengths much more than the past few weeks, but as Caleb Williams showed us in a surgical dissection of the Falcons’ back end, a great one-dimensional attack is still a tough problem to solve. Joe Burrow has 13 touchdowns and and nearly 1,000 yards over the past three games against just three interceptions, and if he’s picked on some lackluster secondaries in Miami and Tennessee in particular, he’s still remarkably dangerous. The fact that he’s throwing to the best wide receiver tandem in football in Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, alongside capable options like tight end Mike Gesicki and running back Samaje Perine, helps his cause a great deal.

The Falcons can and basically have to get pressure to counter this. Burrow can be a wizard in the pocket but in his last full healthy season, he absorbed 48 sacks and can hold on to the ball too long to try to make a play. He’s been excellent against pressure the last two seasons but has thrown four picks under pressure in 2026 and is still markedly worse when pressured than when he has a clean pocket, which makes Atlanta’s attacking front a must. The Falcons need to resign themselves to allowing a few big plays and having a day that’s statistically not super pretty, but if they can force a couple of turnovers and a handful of Burrow misses and throwaways, they can potentially swing the outcome.

Part of that is because the Bengals cannot run the ball. Atlanta’s run defense has been badly exposed the past few weeks, but the Bengals aren’t equipped to take advantage. Chase Brown and Samaje Perine have had league average success rates, roughly, and Brown is averaging a meager 3.5 yards per carry behind a line that has a couple of shaky run blocking options, most notably Amarius Mims. The Bengals will try for some balance, but hopefully that will be a fool’s errand.

If the Falcons can keep Burrow from completely taking over the game, the offense will have to pull its weight. That will start with a major bounceback game from Michael Penix Jr. and the passing game, which just endured an absolute nightmare effort in the rain against the Buccaneers. DJ Turner has been pretty excellent in coverage in 2026 and Kyle Dugger is solid, but the rest of their secondary has struggled with big plays, struggled on a down-to-down basis, or both. Atlanta has a particularly juicy matchup if they can get Kyle Pitts or Bijan Robinson working against linebackers Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter, who have combined to allow 49 completions on 62 targets for 607 yards, or fully one-third of the team’s total allowed passing yards and receptions. The back seven can be picked apart and the defense can be overcome—they just allowed the most points the Titans have scored in five years—should Penix have the time to do so. They do have to watch out for an opportunistic team that has already forced ten fumbles in 2026.

That’s not a given, because Cincinnati’s pass rush has been dangerous. Their interior of the lethal Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, and Kris Jenkins have combined for nine sacks already, and Boye Mafe has another 4.5 coming off the edge. The Falcons will need to be very good on the interior in particular to avoid Lawrence and company blowing up Penix’s pocket, which has reliably led to bad outcomes in 2026, whether those be sacks, fumbles, interceptions, or just costly throwaways.

The remedy to that will be not letting the Bengals pin their ears back, which means running the ball effectively. Fortunately for Atlanta, the Bengals run defense has been merely decent, as they’re 19th in yards, have missed a lot of tackles against opposing run games, and don’t really have any elite run defenders outside of Lawrence. If there was ever going to be a week to get this ground game going again, it would be this one, when the Falcons will badly need to achieve some balance.

The formula here is, once again, clean but complicated to actually execute. If you can slow Burrow and the passing game and take advantage of a talented-but-not-great Cincinnati defense while limiting turnovers, you stand a chance. Falling down in any one of those areas—not being able to run, letting a pressured Penix make costly mistakes, allowing Burrow to really get rolling—likely will mean a rough day in Madrid.

item.title: Chiefs running back Emmett Johnson voted Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week
item.description: Kansas City’s first-year back was the league’s top rookie performer in Week 8.
item.content:encoded:
On Thursday, the NFL congratulated the Kansas City Chiefs rookie running back for being voted Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week.

He was one of four nominees from Week 8, receiving more votes than Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman, Las Vegas Raiders running back Mike Washington Jr. and Los Angeles Rams linebacker Wesley Bailey.

Johnson’s 128 receiving yards were the most by an NFL running back in one game this season (and also the only 100-yard receiving-yard game by any back). He caught five passes and produced 128 yards while running just eight routes. The 73-yard touchdown catch was the longest play by the Chiefs this season.

He also ripped off a highlight-reel 15-yard run that featured a handful of missed tackles forced by the shifty Johnson. That put Johnson’s total yards for the game at 143, the fourth-highest mark by a Chiefs player this year behind lead back Kenneth Walker’s top-3 performances.

This season, Johnson has 314 yards from scrimmage on 34 touches and has moved the chains 11 times. Denver was his breakout performance, and he should be prepared for more opportunity as the season progresses.

Here is the list of previous winners of Rookie of the Week this season:

  • Week 1:Washington Commanders wide receiver Antonio Williams
  • Week 2: Raiders cornerback Hezekiah Masses
  • Week 3:New York Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq
  • Week 4:New York Giants linebacker Arvell Reese
  • Week 5: Jets edge rusher David Bailey
  • Week 6: Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr.
  • Week 7: Omar Cooper Jr.

item.title: AFC North Preview, Week 9: Steelers on bye, Ravens in desperation mode
item.description: Updated Standings: Baltimore Ravens Matchup: vs. Jacksonville Jaguars, 8:15pm EST The Ravens lost their third consecutive game last week and, in the process, lost both of their top quarterbacks to long-term injuries. Lamar Jackson returned only to injure his thumb on the first offensive play, which will place him on IR, while backup Tyler Huntley […]
item.content:encoded:
Updated Standings:

  1. Pittsburgh Steelers 6-2
  2. Cincinnati Bengals 5-2
  3. Cleveland Browns 5-3
  4. Baltimore Ravens 4-4
Baltimore Ravens

Matchup:vs. Jacksonville Jaguars, 8:15pm EST

The Ravens lost their third consecutive game last week and, in the process, lost both of their top quarterbacks to long-term injuries. Lamar Jackson returned only to injure his thumb on the first offensive play, which will place him on IR, while backup Tyler Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury. That left third-stringer Joe Fagnano to play most of the contest against the Bills, which the Ravens lost 36-10.

Now in distress at the quarterback spot, the Ravens will have to try to rally on a short turnaround in a tough matchup against the Jaguars — who are 5-2 with the best point differential in the NFL (+85). The Jaguars’ defense allows the fewest rushing yards per game, which doesn’t’ bode well for a Ravens’ offense that will have to rely heavily on the run game with Fagnano starting. Expect the Ravens to give Fagnano quick outlet passes to prevent him from holding the ball too long given the team’s struggles in pass protection up front.

On the other side of the ball, the Ravens’ defense will be up against it again following consecutive matchups against top-flight offenses (Bengals and Bills). The Jaguars are outside the Top 10 in passing yards and rushing yards, but they score at a high clip (28 points per game) and have a solid group of playmakers. The last couple of weeks have shown that if the Ravens can’t get pressure on the quarterback and finish sacks, their secondary can’t be relied upon to prevent big plays.

Cincinnati Bengals

Matchup:vs. Atlanta Falcons, 9:30am EST (Madrid)

After a signature blowout win over the Ravens in Week 7, the Bengals narrowly escaped a major letdown loss last week against the Tennessee Titans. The Bengals trailed 13-0 in the first quarter and got into a shootout with the Titans and before emerging with a 43-36 overtime victory. It was a good reminder of the team’s offensive explosiveness while also showing they still have defensive flaws and inconsistencies.

This week, the Bengals are traveling to Spain for an international contest against the Falcons. The Falcons are 3-5 and coming off a bizarre 16-0 loss in which their opponent, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, did not complete a pass. The Falcons were shredded for over 300 rushing yards, offering some hope for the Bengals to finally get their run game going in this matchup. So long as Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase continue to play a dominant level, though, it’d be foolish for the Bengals not to keep airing it out to them quite often.

On defense, this is a nice potential spot for the Bengals to force a turnover or two. Michael Penix Jr. tossed four interceptions last week compared to only eight completed passes. The key to limiting the Falcons’ offense begins and ends with Bijan Robinson, who is an all-around weapon in the backfield. Expect the Bengals to load the box on him and pressure Penix, who has struggled against the blitz this season.

Cleveland Browns

Matchup:@ New Orleans Saints, 1:00pm EST

The Browns are heading to New Orleans this week, looking to get back in the win column after a blowout loss in Week 8 against the Steelers (27-6). Cleveland turned the ball over twice and ran for just 34 yards as a team on 15 carries, taking a big step back offensively after scoring 27 points the prior week. They’ll likely have to do without the services of Deshaun Watson (concussion) on Sunday, meaning Shedeur Sanders would start at quarterback.

The Saints are allowing the fourth-most rushing yards per game this season, opening the door for the Browns to have a bounce-back rushing attack performance. They’ll need to establish at least the threat of a run game to support a backup quarterback on the road. Expect Sanders to target tight Harold Fannin often, as the two showed a good connection last year. Fannin is coming off a season-best showing where he caught 10 passes for 154 yards.

Defensively, the Browns can likely afford to prioritize defending the pass. The Saints are a bottom-tier rushing offense and have been riddled with injuries at the running back spot. New Orleans does have an elite wideout in Chris Olave, though, along with some solid supporting pass-catchers. The Browns have been a heavy man coverage defensive team and the Saints are not afraid to take shots downfield.

item.title: NFL Picks Week 9: Sink or Swim
item.description: Week 8 provided some wild finishes and exciting games. Now let’s take a look at what Week 9 will have in store.
item.content:encoded:
The New Orleans Saints return to the field this week, as they come back from their bye to host the Cleveland Browns. Changes were made since the Saints’ loss in Paris, but they were far more minimal than most had hoped. Now we will see if those changes move the needle in a positive direction for the Saints. As the second half of the 2026 season begins, the Saints have to decide if they want to save themselves or not. It is time for the Saints to sink or swim. The swimming needs to start right now, because the waters only get more treacherous after this, and the sinking will occur quickly otherwise.

Let’s take a look at this and all of the exciting NFL action in Week 9.

Last week, I went 11-3

I told you so: Cardinals over Cowboys!

What do I know: Browns over Steelers?

***

WEEK 9

Thursday, November 5th – Thursday Night Football

Jaguars(5-2) at Ravens(4-4)

As the quarterback carousel in Baltimore continues to spin, Trevor Lawrence and the Jags continue to roll. Jacksonville wins 35-24.

Pick: Jaguars

***

Sunday, November 8th – Very Early Game

Bengals(5-2) at* Falcons(3-5) – Madrid, Spain

Joe Burrow will make up for all those completed passes that the Falcons didn’t have to compete with in their shutout loss last week. Cincinnati’s conquest of Atlanta in Spain will be a brutal affair. Cincinnati wins 38-17.

Pick: Bengals

***

Sunday, November 8th – Early Games

Broncos(6-2) at Panthers(3-4)

Carolina is attempting to avoid a three-game losing streak, but they have the misfortune of facing Denver, who is on a four-game winning streak, a streak that may not be challenged until they host Buffalo on Christmas Day. Denver wins 23-21.

Pick: Broncos

***

Cowboys(3-5) at Colts(2-6) 

Following a four-game losing streak and the dismissal of their GM, Indy may be punting on this season, just the opponent Dallas needs, as they hope to keep pace in a very south-like NFC East. Dallas wins 27-21.

Pick: Cowboys

***

Jets(2-6) at Chiefs(5-2)

Kansas City rebounds from a heartbreaking loss in Denver, with a dominating performance against the Jets. Kansas City wins 28-14.

Pick: Chiefs

***

Lions(5-2) at Dolphins(1-6)

After an up and down start to the season, Detroit has found their rhythm over the last month, and that continues in Miami. Detroit wins 30-16.

Pick: Lions

***

Giants(4-2-1) at Eagles(2-6)

Philly is on an astonishing six-game losing streak, a freefall that continues to seven here, despite a spirited fight. New York wins 28-27.

Pick: Giants

***

Rams(4-4) at Commanders(2-4-1)

After an alarming first six weeks of the season, the Rams have begun to right the ship in recent weeks, and that trajectory continues in Washington. Los Angeles wins 28-14.

Pick: Rams

***

Browns(5-3) at Saints(2-5)

Honestly, the Saints haven’t shown they have the coaching or discipline to beat anyone at this point, but a choice is being made here to believe. To believe the Saints can and will win their first home game of the season. To believe they have enough pride as a team to win in the face of so much losing. To believe these players can, for one Sunday, overcome the deficiencies in their coaching, front office, and beyond. For this Sunday, we believe. Saints win 24-17.

Pick: Saints

***

Sunday, November 8th – Late Games

Texans(2-5) at Chargers(0-7)

The two most disappointing teams in the AFC this season face off in this one, but only one of them is truly the worst, and that team is the Bolts. Houston wins 26-14.

Pick: Texans

***

Raiders(4-4) at 49ers(6-1)– Game of the Week

San Francisco comes into this one off their bye week, with the stinging loss in Atlanta still bitter in their mouths, while Vegas is coming off a much-needed win that snapped a four-game slide. On the surface, the Niners should handily win here, but this student (Klint Kubiak) vs. master (Kyle Shanahan) matchup should be an intriguing chess match that will ultimately come down to a game-winning field goal by the home team in the closing moments. San Francisco wins 37-34.

Pick: 49ers

***

Packers(5-3) at Patriots(5-3)

Both of these teams have really found their footing, both having won four of their last five games, but the home team finds a way in the end in this one. New England wins 28-22.

Pick: Patriots

***

Cardinals(3-5) at Seahawks(4-4)

Even without Sam Darnold, Seattle wins this pivotal game behind an inspired defensive performance. Seattle wins 38-14.

Pick: Seahawks

***

Sunday Night Football

Buccaneers(3-5) at Bears(6-2)

The Bucs have had their fun dominating division rivals and not completing passes, but that ends here in the Windy City. It will be surprisingly closer than expected in the final score, but the Bears will win this one. Chicago wins 23-21.

Pick: Bears

***

Monday, November 9th – Monday Night Football

Bills(6-1) at Vikings(6-1)

These division leaders may have equal records, but these teams are not equal. Minnesota’s defense will only carry them so far, then Josh Allen and the Bills will take it from there. Buffalo wins 28-20.

Pick: Bills

***

There you have it, Week 9 is here. Leave us your picks, comments, and insight below!

item.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 9: Latest news, updates on Bhayshul Tuten, Breece Hall, more players for fantasy football
item.description: We go over the NFL injury report going into Week 9, with player updates, news and fantasy football analysis.
item.content:encoded:
Week 9 is the official midway point of the 2026 NFL season. So by now you know what you have on your fantasy football roster. You also know who has been healthy the majority of the year and which players have missed time. The injuries keep coming as we get into the middle of the campaign. As always, we're tracking all the latest news and updates for you, to help with those fantasy football lineups.

NFL Injury Report, Week 9

Quarterback

  • Lamar Jackson, BAL (thumb) — Will be placed on injured reserve

  • Tyler Huntley, BAL (toe) — Reportedly done for the season

  • Kyler Murray, MIN (hamstring)

  • Matthew Stafford, LAR (arm)

  • Sam Darnold, SEA (quad/rib) — Ruled out

  • Deshaun Watson, CLE (concussion protocol)

Ravens QBs: Jackson left in the first half of Sunday's loss to the Bills. He needs surgery on his thumb and is headed for IR. He'll miss at least four games, if not the rest of the season. After Jackson exited, Huntley entered the game and also had to leave due to injury (turf toe), which will end his season. That leaves Baltimore down to third-string rookie Joe Fagnano, who will start against Jacksonville on TNF. Hayden Winks takes a closer look at what Fagnano could bring. The Ravens traded for Jacoby Brissett, but he will not be ready to play this week.

The QB instability is obviously a huge downgrade to the passing game. Fagnano went 10 of 21 for 91 yards and an INT in his first NFL action in Week 8. Zay Flowers is more of a WR3/flex option while Derrick Henry should get a healthy amount of work, though in a tough matchup. Outside of those two, the rest of the Ravens offense should be avoided in fantasy until we see more from Fagnano or the Ravens make a deal for a QB.

Darnold: The Seahawks will be without Darnold in Week 9 against the Cardinals due to quad and rib injuries. With Darnold out, the Seahawks plan to start Drew Lock … who is also dealing with an elbow injury. Lock was excellent when he had to start in place of Darnold against Arizona in Week 2, going 19 of 26 for 235 yards and three touchdowns in a 31-7 win. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 155 yards and three touchdowns in that game, proving JSN is QB-proof and an auto-start again this week.

Running Back

  • Christian McCaffrey, SF (hamstring)

  • Bhayshul Tuten, JAX (ankle/foot) — Game-time decision

  • Jeremiyah Love, ARI (ankle) — Will be placed on IR, miss 4-5 weeks

  • Bam Knight, ARI (concussion)

  • Cam Skattebo, NYG (hamstring)

  • Breece Hall, NYJ (quad) — Expected to be back in Week 9

  • Kyle Monangai, CHI (toe/thumb)

  • David Montgomery, HOU (groin)

  • Travis Etienne Jr., NO (hamstring) — Could be activated off IR

  • TreVeyon Henderson, NE (illness)

  • Brian Robinson Jr., ATL (hamstring)

Tuten: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said the running back will be a game-time decision for Thursday's game against the Ravens. Tuten was a DNP all three days to start the week, with ankle and foot issues. He is coming off his best game of the season. He took 18 touches for 159 yards and two scores in Week 8. Chris Rodriguez Jr. is also dealing with a hand injury but was limited on Monday and Tuesday.

If Tuten is out, Rodriguez gets elevated into the RB2/3 conversation given the Jags are a 10-point favorite. In the rout of the Colts last week, Rodriguez had 58 yards on seven touches and a score. Ameer Abdullah also saw six carries against Indy and could see some work if Tuten is sidelined.

Hall: We thought the Jets were going to get back Hall in Week 8 against the Raiders. That wasn't the case and we got another solid game from Braelon Allen. At this point, even if Hall comes back, expect Allen to be involved given how well he's performed. Allen is the RB5 overall in half-PPR scoring from Weeks 5-8 with Hall sidelined. We'll need to get a look at how the split is in Week 9 with Hall, who got in a limited practice Wednesday, expected back. Plus, it's a tough draw against Kansas City's run defense. But better matchups loom, so don't be surprised if both Hall and Allen are viable RB2/3 options.

Cardinals RBs: Love suffered a new high-ankle sprain in the comeback win over Dallas in OT on Sunday. Knight exited after a big hit and should land in concussion protocol. It'll be tough for Knight to clear in time for Week 9 against the Seahawks, but we'll see. Love has had so many issues with the ankle in his rookie season, and is expected to miss 4-5 weeks while on injured reserve, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. With Love already out, if Knight sits, Tyler Allgeier will be playable, but don't expect 33.6 fantasy points — or anywhere close to that — against Seattle's top defense.

But with Love on IR and Knight starting the season with a lesser role, expect Allgeier to be the lead back moving forward. There could be weeks when Knight is healthy in which the staff rides the hot hand. But Allgeier was brought in to be a high-value backup to Love. Allgeier will have RB2/3 value week-to-week depending on the matchup. Also keep an eye out for James Conner, who is on IR but could be a useful stash.

McCaffrey: CMC comes off the bye navigating a mild hamstring strain. It doesn't feel like this will cause him to miss Week 9 against the Raiders. But we saw before San Francisco's bye that Kyle Shanahan feels comfortable giving the ball to rookie Kaelon Black. We could see more of Black on Sunday to help keep McCaffrey fresh.

Wide Receiver

  • Christian Watson, GB (ribs)

  • Jakobi Meyers, JAX (hamstring/ankle)

  • DeVonta Smith, PHI (hamstring)

  • Michael Wilson, ARI (ribs)

  • Mike Evans, SF (Achilles) — Unlikely to play

  • A.J. Brown, NE (ankle/knee)

  • DJ Moore, BUF (knee)

  • Garrett Wilson, NYJ (concussion protocol)

  • Emeka Egbuka, TB (foot) — Could play in Week 9

  • Jordyn Tyson, NO (hamstring) — Could come off IR

  • Deebo Samuel Sr., SF (hamstring) — Unlikely to play

49ers WRs: Niners GM John Lynch told reporters on Thursday that Evans and Samuel are unlikely to return for Week 9’s matchup against the Raiders. But Demarcus Robinson and KhaDarel Hodge are expected to be back. The expectation was for Evans and Samuel to potentially be back after the Week 8 bye. That doesn’t seem to be the case, so San Fran will be thin at WR again. Robinson’s return is interesting, though we don’t know what to expect from him coming off injury. It was a mixed bag of receivers in Week 7 with Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing and Christian Kirk splitting snaps. George Kittle will remain the primary target for QB Brock Purdy until Evans is back.

Watson: The Packers' lead receiver had a miraculous exit and return to TNF's win over the Panthers in Week 8. Watson finished with an 8-113-0 line on 10 targets, catching a few passes after coming back from the hospital. But Watson revealed he's dealing with a broken rib, which is less than ideal. He'll have ample time to rest before Week 9's matchup with the Patriots. Watson could play through the injury, but if he's active, he would be at risk of exiting the game early. If Watson ends up having to sit, Tucker Kraft and Savion Williams would likely see more targets. Matthew Golden would be elevated into WR1 territory as well.

Wilson: The Cardinals' receiver told reporters after Sunday's win over the Cowboys that he's dealing with broken ribs. It appears Wilson is going to play through the injury. He's a risky option in the flex in PPR formats going up against the Seahawks' stout defense in Week 9.

Egbuka: The Bucs wideout has missed the past two games, and Tampa's passing game sure could use him. The Bucs didn't complete a pass in Week 8's shutout win over the Falcons, instead opting to run the ball 56 times for 324 yards. That likely won't be the case in Chicago in Week 9. If Egbuka can get back — he didn't practice Wednesday — it's a decent matchup, though Tampa Bay ranks dead last in passing offense this season. Egbuka would be a risky flex at best.

Tight End

  • Hunter Henry, NE (foot)

  • Jake Ferguson, DAL (ankle)

  • Colby Parkinson, LAR (ribs)

Ferguson: The Cowboys lost Ferguson to a low-ankle sprain early in the game against Arizona. He didn't return and his status for Week 9 against the Colts could be up in the air. If Ferguson is out, this is still a passing game dominated by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Ryan Flournoy has stepped up as a solid WR3 as well. Brevyn Spann-Ford played 88% of the snaps in Week 8 and had four catches on five targets for 31 yards. In deeper formats, Spann-Ford isn't a bad streamer. He could see garbage-time looks if the Cowboys run away against a struggling Indy team.

item.title: Trade deadline options at cornerback for the Rams
item.description: In the wake of Jaylen Watson injury, where could Rams turn?
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams took a major hit with Jaylen Watson now going on injured reserve due to his shoulder injury. If the Rams want to look outside the facility for another starter at corner, or even just depth, there are a few options out there.

No one Los Angeles can add right now will be as good as Watson has been this year, or at least it’s severely unlikely. According to Next Gen Stats, among outside cornerbacks, Watson entered this past week with the fifth-lowest completion percentage allowed to opposing targets, and is tied for the third-most pass breakups in the league (alongside teammate Quentin Lake). That’s not easy production to replace in general, let alone in the middle of a playoff race.

Still, a few serviceable players are available, even if they will further weaken the Rams’ already limited draft pick pool for 2027.

RIQ WOOLEN

One name that could be available is Riq Woolen, the former Seattle Seahawks corner who hasn’t quite fixed the Philadelphia Eagles’ severe CB2 woes like the latter franchise hoped he would.

Still, Woolen brings size to the table at 6-foot-4 and 210 pounds, which is actually bigger than Watson’s frame (and size is a major selling point for Watson). He hasn’t been great this season, there’s no denying that, but he does have at least a decent track record. He’s also hardly the biggest reason why the Eagles have struggled defensively this year.

Philadelphia has already traded away an offensive contributor and is in a bad spot with a losing record and their starting quarterback unavailable. They’ve turned to Joe Milton at quarterback, which tells you all you need to know. Woolen may not cost too much to acquire, and his contract isn’t completely daunting.

AMIK ROBERTSON

Another NFC East player, Amik Robertson is having a solid season for the 2-4-1 Washington Commanders. He’s a completely different body type than either Woolen or Watson, standing just 5-foot-9 and 183 pounds. This season, Robertson is allowing a 90.3 passer rating as the closest defender, which isn’t spectacular but beggars can’t be choosers if you need a player in a pinch.

It is encouraging that he had one of his best games of the year this past week in a win over the Eagles, allowing a meager 11 yards on four receptions while being targeted six times.

JUJU BRENTS

The Miami Dolphins have had some frisky moments this season, but they’re decidedly not a good football team. They need a ton of help going into next season, and adding a pick in exchange for a cornerback on an expiring rookie contract may be appealing to them.

Similarly, it could appeal to the Rams that Brents is both cheap and playing well as he gears up for his first free agent payday. According to NFL stats whiz Aaron Schatz in commentary for ESPN, Brents is third in coverage DVOA for qualified cornerbacks this year, only behind Jahdae Barron of the Denver Broncos and current Ram Trent McDuffie.

The Rams have enough needs and such little 2027 draft capital that they may decide that promoting from within is the best way to fill the cornerback void long term. But there are options out there if they feel the need to find outside assistance.

item.title: Lion LB Jack Campbell's update was uplifting. His injury was sobering | Opinion
item.description: Lions LB Jack Campbell revealed Nov. 4 that he is continuing to regain movement in his body after a scary on-field injury.
item.content:encoded:
Any given play.

It’s an ultimate NFL reality check. The next snap on a football field could always be the last one, an occupational hazard attached to a brutal, violent sport that can be pure entertainment for millions watching. And pure hell for players willing to risk their bodies for reasons that could include competition, glory, wealth and passion for the game.

Then there’s the other part of that reality, which the Detroit Lions are experiencing with a game looming in Miami on Sunday while Jack Campbell progresses in his recovery from the neck injury that provided the most sobering images from the NFL last weekend: the all-pro linebacker left limp on the turf after a seemingly routine tackle, strapped to a backboard, then taken from the field on a stretcher.

On to the next play.

That’s another occupational challenge, undoubtedly mental amid all the physicality. It’s no wonder that resources the Lions have available at team headquarters, as always now, include counselors. Campbell, 26, went to work at Ford Field and wound up a few miles away at Henry Ford Hospital, and his teammates, some of whom were in tears as medical personnel attended to him, must manage to move on from any trauma.

“It’s a balancing act,” Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters on Wednesday. “You’re humans. And you know it, you want to acknowledge it. It’s a lot, but if that’s weighing that heavy, and that’s where your mind’s at, it’s not going to be good going into this game. And that’s where you get hurt as well.”

The update Wednesday on Jack Campbell – coming from the well-respected team captain himself, in his first public comments since suffering the injury – was uplifting. In an extensive statement released by the team, which previously provided few details of his condition, Campbell said that he has full movement in his lower body and is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body.

Campbell suffered the injury on first play of the fourth quarter, when he and rookie defensive end Eric O’Neill sandwiched Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson on an open-field tackle. As suggested for proper techniques, Campbell made a play with his head upright as it collided with Hockenson’s hip area as he stretched to wrap up the tight end’s legs.

Although specifics of what caused the injury from a medical standpoint have not been publicly revealed, Campbell’s description of his progress confirmed that he does not have paralysis, a worst-case fear when it comes to neck injuries. Seeing Campbell lay motionless on Sunday, though, provided an eerie reminder of the injury suffered in 1991 by Lions guard Mike Utley, left paralyzed from the chest down after a collision on a seemingly routine blocking play.  

And there are too many other cases over the years, from all across the football landscape, where catastrophic injuries changed the course of lives in an instant.

It’s why, regardless of what team you’re rooting for, what fantasy team lineup you’re rolling with or what parlay you’ve bet, there’s humanity in the mix, too. We should never lose sight of that. And that some have paid a heavy toll for, in some cases, being at the wrong place or in the wrong position at the wrong time.

One such case involved another former Lions player, Reggie Brown, whose career as an NFL linebacker ended during the final game of the season in 1997, due to a spinal injury.

“I had my days where I can go to some dark corners in my mind,” Brown, 52, told USA TODAY Sports’ Josh Peter on Monday. “But I have a wife, kids, some real positive things. Kind of just got to go through those emotions and still seek out those things I’m grateful for.”

Campbell, who along with his wife Megan, had their first child in July, also expressed his faith in his statement and asked for continued prayers.

Thank God.

“One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit,” Campbell added, without specifically addressing his football future. “That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge.”

Amen.

His coach’s warning about the team’s mindset, which came with the perspective of playing 11 NFL seasons as a tight end, sounded a lot like his words a little more than two years ago after a Lions victory at Dallas that I happened to cover was soured by a compound fracture suffered by All-Pro defensive end Aidan Hutchinson.

I was struck by the realization expressed by some of the players, echoing the coach, describing how despite the sadness of losing arguably their best player they needed to snap back into focus as a matter of survival after the game was delayed – like Sunday’s – for more than 10 minutes. Such a mindset comes with NFL training.

Unfortunately, they get a lot of practice with this. Yet they are so human, too.

Amon-Ra St. Brown, the star receiver, shared on his podcast that, fittingly, he immediately thought of Campbell’s wife and newborn son, as he processed the scary scene in the moment on Sunday. It was the compassionate reaction.

He knows. For all that his job and sport offers, health is never guaranteed with another NFL reality check one play away.

item.title: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers
item.description: The Buccaneers are coming off two straight wins, including a shutout win over Atlanta.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Bears hype is about to get very loud.

This NFL season seems wide open. There isn't one great team yet and there are few trustworthy contenders who have emerged. The Bears seemingly saw it the same way when they traded two first-round picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

And through one game, it seems like a transformative trade. The Bears had a fantastic performance on a national stage, shutting down the Seahawks in a 34-17 win. Chicago's Super Bowl odds took a leap, as did Caleb Williams' MVP odds. In a season dying for a dominant team to emerge, maybe it's Chicago.

The Bears' offense isn't a question. It has scored 30 points in every game Williams has started and finished (it did score just three points against the Vikings and Williams played three-and-a-half quarters, but that says something about Minnesota's defense). If Simmons has as big of an impact on the defense as it appeared on Monday night, Chicago will be looking really good. Nobody paying attention to the NFL hadn't seen how dominant Simmons is, but it was still impressive to see how quickly he fit in and made plays.

Chicago gets another close-up in prime time this week. They face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night. Surprisingly, the Buccaners are far better analytically than their 3-5 record would suggest. They're fifth in DVOA, eight spots ahead of the Bears, and eight in net EPA (expected points added) per play. The Bears are strong in net EPA, coming in third.

The Buccaneers will be completely overshadowed in this game. The Bears will be the focus on Sunday night as they've emerged as one of the NFL's most dangerous teams. That's a reason they're a healthy 6.5-point favorite. That's a lot of points, and the Buccaneers might be secretly pretty good. That's why Buccaneers +6.5 is the pick. And if the Bears blow out Tampa Bay in a big prime-time window, they'll take over as the talk of the NFL, if they're not already.

Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 9 of the NFL season:

Jaguars (-10) over Ravens

Even at -10, the line seems too low. The Jaguars have three wins by 24 points or more and two came against the 5-3 Browns and the 5-3 Patriots. They're good. There could be a letdown facing Baltimore undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano, and it's possible the Ravens rally around Fagnano for a season-saving performance with Jacoby Brissett on the way next week. But this seems like a huge ask for the Ravens, who have scored 13 or fewer points in three straight games.

Bengals (-3) over Falcons

The Bengals and Falcons go to Madrid, Spain for this one. The Falcons are nearly impossible to figure out. They followed up a win over the undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a pass. That sums up their season. We should trust Joe Burrow, who is on a heater, though there are more questions about Cincinnati's defense after it gave up 36 points to the Titans at home last week.

Giants (-3) over Eagles

Maybe Joe Milton III gives Philadelphia a boost and the Eagles get their first win since Week 2. But since Jalen Hurts went on IR, the Eagles have lost all three games by double digits. It's not a good team in any way, and Milton is far from a sure thing. The Giants are off a bye and should be feeling good coming into this one.

Panthers (+2.5) over Broncos

The Broncos are the better team. A few things work against them in this spot: It's an early start on the East Coast, the Panthers have three days rest advantage and the Broncos are coming off an emotional win over the Chiefs and there could be a letdown. Denver has also been much better at home this season. Carolina has faded after a good start but this is a decent opportunity for a win.

Dolphins (+7) over Lions

Give Miami credit for playing hard. Maybe at some point that effort starts to fade but the last time they truly got blown out was Week 2. They lost by 14 points to the Chiefs, but Kansas City led by only seven points with three minutes left. It's possible the Lions score enough to cover, but remember that they're usually a different team outdoors.

Chiefs (-10) over Jets

Kansas City will enjoy the breather after facing the Seattle and Denver defenses on the road the past two weeks. This seems like the type of game in which the Chiefs could take out their frustrations on an opponent that does have some talent but has won only once since Week 1.

Saints (-3) over Browns

The Browns are likely going with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback because Deshaun Watson was put in concussion protocol. It's not like Watson was playing so well he's irreplaceable, but Sanders has thrown only three passes all season. The Saints are well rested coming off a bye. The Saints are not a great team this season but this might be a spot for them to get right.

Rams (-5.5) over Commanders

Is it time to trust the Rams? They have covered two games in a row without a sweat. Those wins came against mediocre (Raiders) or bad (Chargers) teams, but they did handle business. And the Commanders are mediocre at best and maybe just bad. Let's see if the Rams are truly back.

Cowboys (-5.5) over Colts

It is incredibly hard to trust the Cowboys, especially as a road favorite. But what we saw from the Colts last week in a 42-7 loss was troubling. There was no fight left in that team, which has lost key players to trades and knows its season is done. This could be a bad mistake, trusting a defense that can't stop anyone to cover almost a touchdown on the road. But taking the Colts at this point is even harder.

Texans (-4.5) over Chargers

It's a lot for Houston to be favored by this much on the road, however, home-field advantage has been mostly eliminated this NFL season and the Chargers have no home-field advantage even if that was still a thing. Houston is coming off a bye and still has hopes to revive its season. The Texans still have a 34.4% chance to make the playoffs according to DVOA. The Chargers are 0.0% on that list. They'll cover a spread at some point but it's hard to anticipate it.

Raiders (+10) over 49ers

The Raiders have four losses, and they came against four of the better teams in the NFL: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. The bad news is this week they get the Super Bowl favorites. The 49ers should be getting many players back after their bye. But the Raiders can move the ball and they're getting a lot of points.

Seahawks (-8.5) over Cardinals

WIth all the quarterback chaos this week, we get two teams that had a different quarterback in Week 8. Jacoby Brissett was benched and traded, and Gardner Minshew II takes over. Sam Darnold has a quad injury and he'll be out, with Drew Lock taking over. Lock is a reasonable replacement, and Minshew isn't facing the Cowboys defense this week.

Packers (+3) over Patriots

The Patriots have a lot of injuries and the Packers have a few days of extra rest. In a game that seems evenly matched, the small edges add up. Green Bay started the season very slow but has looked much better over the last four games, winning three and barely losing at Detroit. New England has also emerged after an early-season slump to win four of five. This is a really fun matchup, and even enough to feel OK taking the points.

Vikings (+3.5) over Bills

This is an interesting game because the teams have opposite strengths. The Bills have a great offense and bad defense, and the Vikings have a bad offense and great defense. The Minnesota defense held the Bears to three points after all; Chicago has scored 30 points in every other Caleb WIlliams start. It will be a great test against Josh Allen, who is having another fantastic season. It's never enjoyable to be going against Allen, but getting 3.5 points with a defense this good seems right. As long as the offense does at least a little bit.

WR Notes: Malik Nabers headed into the Giants’ bye week on the back of four-straight 100-yard performances. He could easily make it five vs. an Eagles defense that has waved the white flag on 2026. … Things could not be more annoying for Drake London en route to España. Although Michael Penix Jr. has been “mostly fine,” the Falcons are struggling to attain any passing-game momentum. That includes London being stuck in the Julio Jones netherworld in the red zone, as there seems to be a force field between London and the end zone. Week 9 against the Bengals in Spain would be an excellent place for it to disappear. The Bengals are fresh off getting carved up by Cam Ward, and the bookmakers are preparing for truckloads of points in Madrid. … We hoped Justin Jefferson was getting a year off from his quarterback issues. Instead they’re as bad as ever. Now Jefferson could be going back to Carson Wentz, who, inconceivably, is arguably an upgrade on a hamstring-hobbled Kyler Murray. Say what you will about Wentz, he never pretends he is interested in getting the ball to anyone but his best players. Wentz under center could mean a “low key” fantasy bonanza for Jefferson in Week 9.

Has Chris Olave’s WR1 moment come and gone? He went into the Saints’ bye averaging just 5/48 over his previous three contests, and he could be coming out of it with Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) potentially re-joining the lineup. A large part of Olave’s WR1 appeal over the past calendar year has been his lack of target competition. For Week 9 he will also be facing a Browns pass defense that has remained surprisingly stout without Myles Garrett’s pass-rushing threat. You, of course, never bench Olave. You are also no longer relying on him to be the reason you win your matchup. … The Texans headed into their Week 8 bye with seemingly no idea how they wanted to rotate their receivers in a group that now includes Marvin Harrison Jr. and Tank Dell. That they rotated Nico Collins at all was rather shocking. Hopefully the open date provided reminders that, hey, this Collins guy is pretty good. … Mike Evans (achilles’) failed to resume practicing coming out of the 49ers’ bye week. Then again, Evans has barely practiced even when “healthy” this season. He should be considered genuinely questionable for Sunday’s A+ Raiders matchup, but if he goes, it will be as a player lodged into your WR2 spot.

Rashee Rice’s short-area spamming has become more important than ever to the Chiefs’ undermanned passing attack. You don’t have to like it, but you will probably love it against the Jets’ soft pass defense. … I try to never fall prey to “is the matchup too good?” thinking, but seriously … is the Jags’ Week 9 matchup too good for Parker Washington? The Jags establish whenever possible, and even if Bhayshul Tuten sits in Baltimore, two-score favorites on the road on a short week = the best ever time to try to get the running game established, potentially again limiting the passing volume in an offense with a lot of mouths to feed. … Michael Wilson was the main beneficiary of Week 8’s Minshew Mania. Now he is the most likely victim of the Seahawks’ shutdown pass defense. Last Sunday confirmed Wilson’s continued WR2 status, but no one should be counting on a ceiling effort in Seattle. … DJ Moore was the PPR WR32 in his Week 8 return. Not a terrible outcome when the opposing team’s quarterback gets injured on the first play. “Not a bad outcome” is what you are hoping for again this Monday when the Bills’ take on the Vikings’ ferocious pass defense.

With Zay Flowers you are hoping he gets schemed four first quarter targets from No. 3 QB “Joe Fagnano.” After that, you are on your own in search of cheap PPR points, though there should still be places to find them. … We’ve entered the “well, this is awkward” portion of the Jets’ receiver season. Garrett Wilson was force fed the ball like an alpha No. 1 in Week 8 but could again only watch as someone else had a 100-yard day, this time Adonai Mitchell instead of first-round rookie Omar Cooper Jr. Now Wilson is suddenly concussed and on the wrong side of questionable to face the Chiefs. If Wilson sits, Mitchell and Cooper go from boom/bust WR4s to upside WR2/3s capable of flipping your matchup. … Tre Tucker’s four-catch floor always felt a little too good to be true, and Week 8 proved that was the case. He still has a much higher baseline than most other down-field wideouts in the year 2026. You can keep firing him up as a WR3.

Ladd McConkey is the Chargers’ only good player, and he’s not even that good. For Week 9, he will be facing a Texans defense that really should be better, and almost certainly will be after two weeks to game plan for the league’s most dysfunctional offense. … Shedeur Sanders would equal “advantage KC Concepcion” over Denzel Boston if the check-down king indeed fills in for Deshaun Watson. Not that Watson has made a habit of going deep this season. … DeMario Douglas projects as the only game in town for the Patriots’ receiver corps, though Mack Hollins (calf, injured reserve) is pushing to join him. Even if Hollins plays, Douglas will have a WR4 floor. Without Hollins in the lineup, Douglas can scrape by as a WR3. … Makai Lemon keeps doing the bare minimum. That will be put to the test with No. 3 QB Joe Milton taking over for No. 2 Tanner McKee, but easy Lemon looks remain the most sensible thing for his beleaguered offense to scheme up at the moment. … With Emeka Egbuka (foot) yet to resume practicing and the Bucs having made it clear they will run the ball whenever fate/chance/circumstance allows, there is no Bucs wideout worth a WR3 flier despite a potential shootout spot with the Bears.

RB Notes: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) is not practicing to begin the week. We ultimately expect him to be out there against the Raiders, but perhaps Kyle Shanahan will give his lead back another week to get right with the Niners two-score favorites vs. the Silver and Black. In the event of a CMC no-show, Kaelon Black would become a must-start option. Even now, Black is a solid FLEX in a game that could have lots of clean-up time. … Bhayshul Tuten has been setting up breakout pins to be knocked down for weeks now, but the RB1 coronation appears on hold for Thursday evening’s short-week date with two-score underdog Baltimore. Even if Tuten does play through his foot and ankle issues, why would you give him a full workload when the other team's starting quarterback is a UDFA out of UConn? Tuten is now an uncertain RB2, with Chris Rodriguez Jr. a must-play FLEX even if Tuten suits up. … TreVeyon Henderson has now remained sidelined for more than a week with an illness. Hopefully it’s just a case of the trade deadline flu, because otherwise that would be highly unusual and a sign of something actually serious. Whatever it is, Henderson appears unlikely to face the Packers. That leaves 18-20 touches for Rhamondre Stevenson in what should be a back-and-forth affair with the Packers.

Braleon Allen has played so well for so long during Breece Hall’s injury that it is tempting to believe there is no way the Jets could go back to their old committee status quo, but that is frequently the disappointing outcome in these situations. We will give Allen a one-week benefit of the doubt period, but he has fallen from borderline RB1 to more uncertain RB2. … As for Hall, it is best to treat him as an Ashton Jeanty type. No longer the clear-cut leader on early downs, but a high-value touch magnet in the passing game. He’s in the RB2/3 mix, with ample room to grow ahead of Week 10. … It’s taken a lot, but it appears Tyler Allgeier is getting something of a last fantasy laugh in the Cardinals’ backfield, right down to the Birds making a quarterback change in time for one of the toughest road trips an NFL team can make. With Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight out and Gardner Minshew starting, it would be an enormous upset were Allgeier to finish with fewer than 18 touches. That puts you on the RB2 map. Let’s see if he can stay there.

It would appear Sean Payton has finally stopped messing around in his backfield. Jonah Coleman led in every meaningful Week 8 category, and is actually producing, unlike J.K. Dobbins. Things tend to change quickly in Payton’s world, but the Coleman we saw in Week 8 was an RB2. … As for Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr., I believe several things happened in Week 8: Washington missed his shot, and Jeanty got the message. The Raiders were more than willing to let MWJ run away with early-down duties. Only he didn’t run away from anybody behind the Raiders’ hideous run blocking. Jeanty, meanwhile, actually made the most of his extremely limited workload, and still maintained the lead in passing situations. More likely to force more of a timeshare on early downs instead of repeating last week’s 25-2 disaster, Jeanty gets one more week ahead of Washington in the ranks. … David Montgomery (groin) has already been declared out for Week 9, leaving the Woody Marks one man band intact against the Chargers. With the Texans road favorites against the dazed Bolts, Marks should at least receive an RB2 workload. Whether he turns it into RB2 returns is another question.

The Vikings’ Week 8 backfield could not have been less satisfying if it tried. Neither Aaron Jones nor Jordan Mason reached 40 percent of the Vikes’ snaps in a slobberknocker with the Lions, while DeeJay Dallas was somehow on the field more frequently than Mason. That points in the direction of a continued Jones advantage when it comes to overall work and high-value touches, but he is not somebody you would feel good about in your RB2 spot. … The Seahawks’ backfield has become enough of a fantasy quagmire that it is tempting to boil it down to its basest elements, such as — who is the best player? It’s probably Jadarian Price, but “probably” tends not to get you very far in the Mad Max wasteland that is the current RBFLEX landscape. The most likely “probably” is a do-over of the Seahawks’ Week 8 approach. Keep spreading the ball around and see what it happens, especially with starting QB Sam Darnold down for a date with the lowly, road-tripping, quarterback-changing Cardinals. As such, we can’t make any strong recommendations, but we also can’t rule out the likes of Zach Charbonnet.

Speaking Wednesday, Bucs coach Todd Bowles claimed Kenneth Gainwell’s recent production has the Bucs’ backfield much closer to the 1A/1B ordeal fantasy managers feared over the summer. While that cannot be completely ruled out, I still think it is a safer bet Gainwell was the beneficiary of back-to-back unrepeatable game scripts. And for as well as Gainwell played, Bucky Irving was much better. I’m not letting Bowles’ comments scare me off Irving, and I also won’t let them talk me into starting Gainwell. … I wouldn’t typically be typing up reasons to start the Browns’ change-of-pace running back, but with Deshaun Watson (concussion) likely to sit, check-down king Shedeur Sanders could develop quite the repartee with third-down option Dylan Sampson. … The Chargers still had a full-blown three-man backfield committee coming out of their bye week. Omarion Hampton “led” with 11 touches but played fewer snaps than both Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell. Hampton continues to default into the “highest” rank, but highest in this case should be outside most FLEX spots. … It was about time Emmett Johnson got more involved as a pass catcher. Alas, he actually played his fewest snaps of the season and did not see an increase in routes. Aka, it is quite possible it was a fluke. We can at least hope it was a fluke that opened some Chiefs coaching staff eyes.
